metadata.description: Enterprise landing zone configuration for large organizations with complex requirements

questions.text: What is your organization's name?
questions.help_text: This will be used in account names and resource tags

questions.text: Where is your organization primarily based?
questions.help_text: Tell me your primary location - I'll recommend the best AWS region

inference.hint: Map user's location to the nearest AWS region that supports Control Tower. Consider: geographic proximity, data residency requirements, and service availability. Common mappings: UK/London → eu-west-2, Australia/Sydney → ap-southeast-2, US East Coast → us-east-1, US West Coast → us-west-2, Germany/Netherlands → eu-central-1, Singapore/Southeast Asia → ap-southeast-1, Japan → ap-northeast-1, Canada → ca-central-1
inference.validation_note: MUST store a valid AWS region CODE (e.g., eu-west-2, us-east-1, ap-southeast-2). Do the location->region mapping yourself and record ONLY the region code as home_region -- NEVER store the user's raw city/country/phrase. If the location is ambiguous (e.g. 'Washington' = WA state vs Washington DC), ask the user which region. A non-region value is rejected by the generator (issue #110).

questions.presentation_template: Based on your location, I recommend **{{value}}** ({{region_label}}) as your home region for Control Tower and centralized services.

questions.text: What type of enterprise organization are you?
questions.help_text: Tell me your industry sector - this helps configure appropriate compliance and security controls

inference.hint: Classify organization by industry: 'bank/financial services' → financial, 'hospital/healthcare/pharma' → healthcare, 'retail/ecommerce/shopping' → retail, 'factory/manufacturing/industrial' → manufacturing, 'software/saas/tech' → technology, 'media/entertainment/publishing' → media, 'energy/utilities/power' → energy, anything else → other

questions.presentation_template: Based on your industry ({{industry_description}}), I'll classify this as **{{type_label}}** and configure appropriate {{compliance_note}}.

compliance_notes.financial: PCI DSS and SOX compliance controls
compliance_notes.retail: PCI DSS compliance for payment processing

questions.text: How many employees does your organization have?
questions.help_text: Helps determine appropriate account structure and support requirements
questions.presentation_template: With {{employee_description}}, I classify this as **{{scale_label}}** which means {{infrastructure_note}}.

infrastructure_notes.under_1000: streamlined account structure with essential infrastructure
infrastructure_notes.1000_10000: comprehensive account structure with dedicated infrastructure accounts
infrastructure_notes.10000_50000: complex account structure with business unit separation
infrastructure_notes.over_50000: highly distributed account structure with regional and BU organization

questions.text: How many AWS accounts do you anticipate managing?
questions.help_text: Determines account vending and governance automation requirements

questions.text: What is your geographic distribution?
questions.help_text: Determines multi-region networking and compliance requirements

sections.name: Operational Model
sections.description: IT structure and cloud operating model

questions.text: How is your IT organization structured?
questions.help_text: Determines account organization and delegation model

questions.text: How is your cloud team structured?

options.label: Embedded cloud teams in business units

questions.help_text: Determines SCPs, guardrails, and delegation boundaries

questions.text: What's your team's AWS/cloud experience and maturity?
questions.help_text: Describe your cloud journey and current capabilities

inference.hint: Classify cloud maturity: 'just started/exploring/new to cloud' → beginning, 'some workloads/building capabilities' → developing, 'established governance/scaling adoption' → advancing, 'optimizing/cloud-native' → mature, 'driving innovation/best practices' → leading

questions.presentation_template: Based on {{maturity_description}}, I classify your maturity as **{{level_label}}**. This means {{automation_note}}.

automation_notes.beginning: we'll use proven patterns with comprehensive documentation
automation_notes.developing: we'll include automation while maintaining visibility
automation_notes.advancing: we can use advanced automation and self-service capabilities
automation_notes.mature: we'll enable sophisticated DevOps and GitOps patterns
automation_notes.leading: we can implement cutting-edge cloud-native architectures

questions.text: Do you need a dedicated Network account?
questions.help_text: Strongly recommended for enterprise - centralized network management

questions.text: Do you need a SharedServices account?
questions.help_text: Recommended for hosting shared resources like Active Directory, DNS

questions.text: Do you need a Monitoring account?
questions.help_text: Recommended for centralized observability and SIEM integration

questions.text: Beyond the standard OUs (Infrastructure, Workloads, Sandbox, Exceptions, Development, Production — Security is set up by Control Tower), what additional OUs do you need?
questions.help_text: Comma-separated list (e.g., 'Development, Production, BusinessUnit-A')

questions.text: What are your on-premises connectivity requirements?

options.label: Direct Connect to one or more regions

questions.help_text: Determines hybrid networking architecture

questions.text: What are your multi-region networking requirements?
questions.help_text: Determines Transit Gateway and network architecture complexity

questions.text: Do you need centralized network inspection with AWS Network Firewall?
questions.help_text: Recommended for enterprise - centralized network security

questions.text: Should default VPCs be deleted?
questions.help_text: Recommended - removes insecure default configurations

questions.text: Do you want to deploy hybrid DNS (Route 53 Resolver) to forward DNS between AWS and your on-premises network?
questions.help_text: Deploys inbound/outbound Route 53 Resolver endpoints in the Network account with a FORWARD rule to your on-prem DNS, shared org-wide. Requires a dedicated Network account. Only enable if you have on-premises DNS servers to integrate with. Cost: ~$0.125/hr per resolver endpoint ENI (two ENIs per endpoint) plus $0.40 per million queries.

questions.text: Which on-premises DNS domains should be forwarded from AWS? Enter a comma-separated list (e.g. corp.example.com, internal.example.com).
questions.help_text: DNS queries for these domains are forwarded from AWS to your on-premises DNS servers via the outbound resolver endpoint.

questions.text: What are your on-premises DNS server IP addresses? Enter a comma-separated list (e.g. 192.168.1.10, 192.168.1.11).
questions.help_text: The target DNS servers the FORWARD rule sends queries to. Must be reachable from the Network account VPC over your hybrid connection.

questions.text: Which source CIDR ranges may send DNS queries to the inbound resolver? Enter a comma-separated list (e.g. 192.168.0.0/16, 10.0.0.0/8).
questions.help_text: On-premises networks allowed to resolve AWS private DNS via the inbound resolver endpoint's security group.

questions.text: What is your security operations approach?
questions.help_text: Determines security tool integration and alerting

questions.text: What level of security automation have you implemented?
questions.help_text: Determines automation and response capabilities

questions.text: Should IAM user creation be prevented (SSO-only)?
questions.help_text: Recommended for enterprise - enforces SSO/Identity Center

questions.text: Should public S3 buckets be prevented?
questions.help_text: Recommended - blocks publicly accessible buckets

questions.text: Do you want to restrict which AWS regions can be used?
questions.help_text: Recommended for compliance and cost control

questions.text: Which geographic areas should be allowed?
questions.help_text: Describe geographic requirements - I'll map to AWS regions. Important: these must be a subset of the regions your existing Control Tower landing zone already governs - org-wide StackSets (e.g. EBS encryption) cannot deploy to a region Control Tower does not govern. Check your governed regions in the Control Tower console (Landing zone settings) or via 'aws controltower get-landing-zone'.

inference.hint: Map geographic descriptions to AWS region code arrays. 'Europe' or 'EU' → [eu-west-1, eu-west-2, eu-central-1, eu-north-1]. 'US' or 'United States' → [us-east-1, us-east-2, us-west-1, us-west-2]. 'Asia Pacific' or 'APAC' → [ap-southeast-1, ap-southeast-2, ap-south-1, ap-northeast-1]. Include home region. Be inclusive - if user says 'Europe', include all European regions.
inference.validation_note: Must output array of valid AWS region codes

questions.text: Enable VPC Flow Logs?
questions.help_text: Recommended for security and troubleshooting

questions.text: VPC Flow Logs for the centralized Inspection/Egress VPC are delivered to the central S3 bucket in the Log Archive account. Confirm S3 as the destination.
questions.help_text: The landing zone centralizes flow logs to the Log Archive S3 bucket, which is cost-effective for long-term storage. CloudWatch Logs delivery is not offered for the centralized Inspection/Egress VPC; enable CloudWatch flow logs per workload VPC/account after deployment if you need real-time queries.

questions.text: How long should logs be retained?
questions.help_text: Longer retention for compliance and forensics

questions.text: Backup frequency?

questions.text: Backup retention period?
questions.help_text: Based on RPO/RTO and compliance requirements

sections.name: Account Email Addresses
sections.description: Email configuration for AWS accounts. IMPORTANT: Each email must be globally unique across ALL of AWS. Plus-addressed emails (user+tag@domain.com) often collide. Use dedicated mailboxes or distribution lists. Failed account creation leaves retained (orphaned) accounts that cannot be rolled back.

questions.help_text: Must be globally unique across AWS. Avoid plus-addressed emails as they often collide. Use a dedicated mailbox.
